said.usage: usage: miyu onebot start | stop | restart | status | logs [-f] | web [--print] | venue show <venue> (serve is started by the core only)
said.no-log: The run log cannot be written: {reason}
said.notice/disconnected: NapCat disconnected; waiting for it to reconnect.
said.notice/disconnected-as: NapCat disconnected ({bot}); waiting for it to reconnect.
said.failure/port-in-use: Port {port} is in use. Pick another: miyu config set --system onebot.listen <port>, and change NapCat to match.
said.failure/crashed: The QQ bridge hit a bug and stops: {reason}
said.failure/start: The QQ bridge could not start: {reason}
said.notice/no-token: No token (onebot.token) yet, so NapCat will be refused. Generate one on the Connection page of the web UI and put it into NapCat; it connects within seconds.
said.notice/web: The QQ bridge web page is at http://127.0.0.1:{port}; open it with miyu-onebot web.
said.failure/web-port-in-use: Port {port} is in use. Pick another: miyu config set --system onebot.web <port>.
said.open/not-running: No QQ bridge web page on 127.0.0.1:{port}. Turn it on with miyu onebot start.
said.open/first: No web password yet: opening the web page with a one-time code to set a username and password.
said.open/opened: The QQ bridge web page is at {url} and has been opened in your browser.
said.open/print-hint: If the browser did not open, use miyu-onebot web --print.
said.open/code-warning: This link works once within 5 minutes. Do not share it.
said.failure/not-spawned: No handshake reply from the core. miyu-onebot serve is started by the core only: turn the QQ bridge on with miyu onebot start.
said.control/started: The QQ bridge is on: the core starts it now and every time the core starts.
said.control/stopped: The QQ bridge is off: the core stopped it and will not start it again.
said.status/off: The QQ bridge is off. Turn it on with miyu onebot start.
said.status/waiting: The QQ bridge exited; it starts again in {seconds} s ({failures} failures in a row).
said.status/stopped: The QQ bridge stopped and the core will not start it again: {reason}
said.status/stderr: The last lines of its standard error:
said.status/missing: The core has no onebot package: its manifest is missing or wrong; check it with miyu check.
said.status/ports: NapCat connects to ws://127.0.0.1:{listen}/ws; the web page is at http://127.0.0.1:{web} (open it with miyu onebot web).
said.reason/config_error: a configuration error or a port in use (exit code 1). Fix it, then run miyu onebot restart.
said.reason/failed_repeatedly: it failed {failures} times in a row. See miyu onebot logs, then run miyu onebot restart.
said.reason/not_installed: there is no miyu-onebot program next to miyu.
said.reason/cannot_start: it could not be started: the system refused, or its directory or standard error file could not be made.
said.reason/protocol_mismatch: its manifest speaks a protocol version the core does not.
said.failure/factory: The QQ bridge cannot start: its factory data has problems (a packaging error):
said.venue/none: No rule sets anything for this venue.
said.venue/defaults: Parameters not listed follow the factory defaults.toml.
said.venue/problems: Problems found while reading (the wrong item, rule or file is not used; the rest is):
said.venue/bad-venue: Not a venue id: {venue}. Write <platform>:group:<group> or <platform>:private:<user>, for example qq:group:123456.
said.problem/not-an-option: {key} is not one of the options: {got}
said.group/rate-limited: Too many calls right now; please try again in a few minutes.
said.web/login/no-password: No password yet? Run miyu-onebot web in a terminal.
said.web/setup/hint: This is your Miyu web account: sign in with it here and in the Miyu web UI.
said.web/token/confirm: NapCat will need the new token as well. Change it?
said.web/guide/token: Generate a token: press Generate in the Access token row below.
said.web/guide/napcat: In NapCat's network settings, add a WebSocket client with the URL and token below, and choose Array as the message format.
said.web/guide/wait: Wait a few seconds until NapCat below shows Connected.
said.web/ports/listen-moved: NapCat's port is now {port}: change the URL in NapCat to the one above.
said.web/ports/web-moved: The web UI moved to port {port} and opens there now. Sign-ins are kept per address, so sign in again at the new one.
said.web/ports/in-use: Port {port} is in use, so the bridge keeps its old ports. Pick another one and save again.
said.web/people/owners/hint: Private chats from these accounts are the local account itself; in groups they also get the admin commands.
said.web/people/owners/empty: No owners yet. Press Add, enter your own QQ number and press Save: from then on she knows it is you in private chat.
said.web/people/trusted/hint: They can call her in private chat, with no rate limit, even while she sleeps.
said.web/people/trusted/later: The QQ bridge uses this list once groups are connected; it is kept until then.
said.web/people/risk/title: An owner account is you: know these three costs
said.web/people/risk/stolen: If the QQ account is stolen, someone else uses this machine with your permissions.
said.web/people/risk/forged: "This is from the owner" rests on what NapCat reports: a compromised or malicious NapCat can fake your private chats.
said.web/people/risk/injection: Prompt injection hidden in web pages or files can make her change workspace files within what the sandbox allows; nothing beyond the sandbox can be done from a private chat.
